plain_english_policy: This bill authorizes public four-year colleges and universities in Alabama to hold board of trustees meetings (and their committees) via telephone or video conference. For these remote participation methods to be valid, the institution must provide notice according to the Open Meetings Act and allow members of the public to simultaneously listen to or observe the meeting.
policy_direction_if_enacted: Enactment would legally permit university boards in Alabama to conduct official business remotely using audio/video technology. This changes policy by expanding procedural flexibility for governance meetings, provided that transparency requirements (notice under the Open Meetings Act and simultaneous public access) are met.
sponsorship_supports_position: Senator Figures advanced this bill to authorize remote participation in university board meetings under specific transparency conditions.
evidence_quotes: "This bill would allow the board of trustees... or any other committee established by a board of trustees of any public four-year institution of higher education in this state to participate in meetings by telephone conference or video conference if notice of the meetings is given pursuant to the Open Meetings Act and the members of the public are given the opportunity to simultaneously listen to or observe such meetings."

"Members of the board of trustees... may participate in a meeting of the board or committee by means of telephone conference, video conference, or similar communications equipment by means of which all persons participating in the meeting may hear each other at the same time. Participation by such means shall constitute presence in person at a meeting for all purposes, including the establishment of a quorum."
